Hey Mark, have you thought about when we should hold the meeting in July? I was thinking... July 9 might be a good date. What do you think? 

Also, I've been curious about your stance on army rule. What's your opinion on that?

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark

July 9... well, it could work. But maybe we should consider the schedules of everyone involved. A little more flexibility might help.

As for army rule, I think it's a bad idea. It just leads to more issues than solutions. I've seen how it affects people. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:

Regarding army rule, I see it differently. I believe it can provide stability and security. It’s not all bad; there are some benefits too. What makes you feel so strongly against it?

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark

shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
I see your concern about attendance, but July 9 allows us to proceed without unnecessary delays. We can always work around individual schedules later.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message: No, that's not how it works. Army rule doesn't safeguard rights; it actually strips people of their freedoms. Properly speaking, strong governance should come from democracy, not from military force. It's naive to think that restrictions can maintain order without causing more harm. In our way, we value individual rights and autonomy over authoritarian control. What you're describing sounds more like oppression than stability.
